name: Long Strangle
summary: Buy an OTM call and an OTM put in the same expiry; a cheaper, wider-breakeven version of the long straddle that needs a bigger move.

legs.strike_rule: OTM put at 0.20-0.30 delta, symmetric in delta rather than in dollars (put skew makes dollar-symmetry wrong).

max_profit: unlimited upside; (put strike * 100) - debit on the downside
max_loss: net debit paid, realized if the underlying finishes between the two strikes
breakevens: call strike + total debit per share, and put strike - total debit per share

greeks.delta: near zero at entry if chosen by matching deltas
greeks.gamma: positive but lower than a straddle
greeks.theta: negative, less severe per dollar than a straddle but proportionally similar
greeks.vega: strongly positive; the best pure long-vega expression per dollar in this family

typical_dte: 30-60 DTE. Strangles need time because they need a big move.
when_to_use: IV rank <= 20 and an expectation of a regime change in volatility, or a known binary catalyst where the expected move exceeds the strike distance. Prefer over a straddle when you want maximum vega per dollar and are willing to accept a wider dead zone.
entry_rules: IV rank <= 20 over 252 days. This is a long-vega trade; buy vol when it is objectively cheap.
Both legs 0.20-0.30 delta, chosen by delta not by equal dollar distance.
Total debit <= 1.0% of equity per position ($500 on $50k).
Move check: (call strike - put strike + debit)/spot must be <= the largest 30-day range over the last 12 months; if the required move has never happened, do not buy it.
DTE 30-60. Never open a strangle under 21 DTE without a dated catalyst.
IV30 < HV20 - 3 vol points, or a catalyst inside the expiry with >= 5 days of cushion after it.
Both legs OI >= 500, bid/ask <= 10% of mid.
management_rules: Take profit at +50% of debit, or when one leg alone can be sold for more than the total debit paid.
Time stop: close at 21 DTE if not at target. Theta on OTM options accelerates hard in the last three weeks.
Vol stop: close if IV rank rises above 50 and price has not moved -- you got the vol expansion without the move; take the vega profit.
If one side goes deep ITM (delta > 0.80), consider selling that leg and holding the cheap wing as a free lottery ticket, but only if the remaining leg's value is < 10% of realized profit.
exit_rules: Flat by 15:45 ET on expiration day.
No short legs, so no assignment risk. But OCC auto-exercises long options $0.01 ITM at expiry, which would create unwanted stock. Close both legs before 15:45 ET every expiration.
Close the whole structure at 21 DTE absent a catalyst.
assignment_risk: None -- both legs are long. The only stock-delivery risk is OCC auto-exercise of your own ITM long leg at expiry, prevented by closing before 15:45 ET.
liquidity_needs: OI >= 500 per leg. OTM wings on less-liquid names quote badly; restrict to underlyings with at least 5,000 contracts of daily option volume.
common_mistakes: Buying strangles at elevated IV and calling it a 'cheap' trade; choosing strikes by equal dollar distance instead of equal delta (skew makes this lopsided); holding into the last three weeks; sizing as if the max loss is unlikely -- for strangles, max loss is the modal outcome.
zero_dte_notes: A 0DTE strangle needs an enormous intraday move to clear two OTM premiums plus slippage. Statistically a loser except on scheduled macro prints, and even then a 0DTE straddle is the better expression. Mark as not enabled.
family: Two-leg verticals and same-expiry two-leg combos (call/put verticals, straddles, strangles, guts, synthetics/risk reversals, ratio verticals and backspreads)
